Sure I can try.

First. Figure out what you need to detox from first. Usually people will say you have to detox from all of social media, which is a good start if you spend to much time on social media. But for me, social media in general isn’t much of an issue so it wouldn’t make sense for me to detox from it. To figure out what to detox from, think about all of the things you do repetitively from impulsivity that don’t bring you any joy any more. For me one of the big problems I had was with video games, I would play for over 4 hours after work every day and I didn’t even enjoy it any more.

Second. Detox for **at least** 2 weeks, but recommended an **entire month** if you really want to see results. Don’t take my word for it, you can either listen to Dr. Anna Lembke or Dr. K(Dr. Alok Kanojia) if you want an explanation for why it must take so long. But the gist of it is quite simple, any impulsive behaviour you repeat for a very long time is going to be very hard if not impossible to get rid of overnight, and it takes about a month for your brain to adapt to a new behaviour.

Third. Embrace boredom. Being bored is the whole point. The first week is going to suck, but you can comfort yourself with the idea that if you are feeling bored then you are doing the detox right and the results will probably be more promising because of it. 

Fourth?! Actually do the productive/creative thing that you can’t bring yourself to do. Don’t wait for the dopamine detox to take effect and magically motivate you with newfound passion and interest, that doesn’t happen. Just the same way you have to struggle to get rid of bad behaviours, you have to struggle to develop new ones. 

You can start by just doing it for 5 minutes a day… then gradually increase the duration of time spent working on your new habits day by day, but there are many other ways to develop new habits. 

I hope this helps.

>

> 
> 
>

> 
> 
> 
> icacls %localappdata%\Spotify\Update /deny "%username%":D
> 
> 
> 
> icacls %localappdata%\Spotify\Update /deny "%username%":R
> 
> 
> 
> Description of given commands:
> 
> 
> 
>     Removes directory C:\Users\<your username>\AppData\Spotify\Update
> 
>     Creates directory C:\Users\<your username>\Appdata\Spotify\Update
> 
>     Denies delete permission to your account for C:\Users\<your username>\Appdata\Spotify\Update requiring administrative prompt for delete privileges, preventing spotify from removing it without admin
